overview.problemStatement: wirekit has no OAuth2 helper. wirekit::google_lsa works but takes a bare access token the caller obtained elsewhere, so every future Google module would re-implement authorization URLs, PKCE, code exchange, refresh, and revocation. That duplication is where the security errors live: an implicit flow slipping in, a missing PKCE verifier, a reused state value, a refresh loop on 401, a token cached past expiry. catalogue/28_google_oauth.md specifies the module and CON-212 already requires Authorization Code + PKCE, but nothing implements it.
overview.proposedSolution: Add wirekit::google_oauth behind an additive google-oauth feature: GoogleOAuthClient (client id/secret, redirect URI, scopes), AuthorizationRequest (URL, state, PKCE challenge), TokenResponse (access, refresh, expiry, scope), a TokenStore trait, and RevokeRequest. The module builds authorization URLs, exchanges codes, refreshes access tokens, revokes them, and validates state and PKCE. wirekit performs no I/O and stores nothing (CON-108), so the crate ships the TokenStore trait and an in-memory implementation; durable encrypted persistence is the implementor's documented contract. google_lsa accepts the helper as a token source while keeping a static-token path.
overview.targetAudience: Primary: external Rust developers connecting a Google account from a server process who need PKCE, refresh, and revocation correct without re-deriving OAuth. Secondary: maintainers of this workspace, who need one auth path shared by every Google module.
assumptions: wirekit core (BP-005) is on main after m1-first-publish archived; the exact WirekitError::Auth variants available are [to be confirmed].
One Google Cloud project serves all callers; per-tenant apps are out of scope (catalogue open question 1).
Google's oauth2.googleapis.com contract is as documented in catalogue/28; no task here uses a live Google account.
No external research was available; every claim comes from the catalogue, the constitution, and the existing wirekit source.
outOfScope: Reading, writing, encrypting, or rotating tokens on disk: TokenStore is a trait
Google Business Profile, Gmail, and LSA notification modules themselves
Per-tenant Google Cloud projects, app verification, and branding review
Incremental-consent UX beyond the scope set the caller supplies
Application UI, product nouns, and billing (CON-106)
Test authoring and execution (/sdrive:test owns them)

userStories.title: Start a Google authorization safely
userStories.want: an authorization URL with state and PKCE
userStories.benefit: a stolen callback cannot be replayed or forged

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a client id, redirect URI, and scope set, when authorization_url is called, then the URL targets https://oauth2.googleapis.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth with response_type=code, the scopes, the redirect URI, a random state, and code_challenge with code_challenge_method=S256.
Given the returned request, when the same client builds another, then state and code_verifier differ, and neither is derived from the client secret.
Given a caller asks for the implicit flow, when the request is built, then no such option exists in the API because there is no parameter that omits PKCE.

userStories.title: Exchange, refresh, and revoke
userStories.want: code exchange, refresh on expiry, and revocation

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a valid code and matching verifier, when exchange_code runs, then it POSTs the code and verifier to the token endpoint and returns a typed TokenResponse with access token, optional refresh token, absolute expiry, and scopes.
Given the endpoint answers 400 with an error and error_description body, when the exchange fails, then the error is WirekitError::Auth carrying the provider code and no token is returned.
Given a stored token past expiry minus the safety margin, when a token is requested, then exactly one refresh occurs, the store is updated, and a second 401 fails without a second attempt.
Given a refresh token, when revoke runs, then the revocation endpoint is called once and the store record is removed.

userStories.title: Keep credentials out of logs and state out of the library
userStories.want: the secret and tokens never rendered and no persistence inside the library
userStories.benefit: the blast radius of a log line or a crash is bounded

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a client, a TokenResponse, and every error path, when Debug, Display, tracing, and error payloads are inspected, then the client secret, access token, and refresh token render ***, and their types do not implement Serialize.

Given the crate is compiled, when its dependencies are inspected, then it performs no file, database, environment, or network read or write beyond the OAuth endpoints, and a TokenStore implementation is supplied by the caller.

functionalRequirements.text: wirekit MUST provide google_oauth::{GoogleOAuthClient, AuthorizationRequest, TokenResponse, TokenStore, RevokeRequest} behind an additive google-oauth feature that is default-off and enables no other feature.

authorization_url MUST build a URL against https://oauth2.googleapis.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth carrying response_type=code, the caller's scopes, the redirect URI, a CSPRNG state, and a code_challenge derived from a freshly generated verifier using S256.
The API MUST NOT offer a way to omit PKCE or to use the implicit flow; CON-212 is enforced by the type, not by documentation.

exchange_code MUST POST the code and verifier to https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token and MUST return a typed TokenResponse whose expiry is absolute, computed from the provider's expires_in and the caller's clock source.

The module MUST map Google's error and error_description into WirekitError::Auth for credential and request failures and WirekitError::Api for provider-side failures, preserving the provider code (CON-207).
Token acquisition MUST refresh at most once on 401, MUST persist the refreshed token through the TokenStore trait, and MUST fail rather than loop (CON-208).
revoke MUST call the revocation endpoint once and MUST remove the record through the TokenStore.
TokenStore MUST be a trait with object-safe load, save, and delete operations, and the crate MUST ship an in-memory implementation for tests and single-process callers.

The module MUST accept a configurable token endpoint base URL for sandbox and test use, MUST default to the documented Google endpoint, and MUST reject a non-HTTPS override unless it is loopback and explicitly allowed (CON-520).

The client secret, access token, and refresh token MUST be held in the wirekit secret type, MUST render *** in Debug, Display, tracing, and errors, and their types MUST NOT implement Serialize (CON-214).
The module MUST emit tracing events for authorization, exchange, refresh, revoke, and every error, and MUST NOT record a token, verifier, or secret (CON-211).
wirekit::google_lsa MUST accept a GoogleOAuthClient token source instead of a bare token string, and MUST keep working for callers that supply a static token.

nonFunctionalRequirements.text: Credentials MUST come from the caller at construction; none may be embedded, defaulted, or read from the environment (CON-511, CON-519).
No global or static token cache; every client owns its own state (CON-109, CON-512).
The token endpoint MUST be rate-limited through the shared bucket with a caller override (CON-209, CON-514).
Every untrusted input - provider error bodies, redirect parameters, scope strings - MUST be validated and MUST produce a typed error rather than a panic (CON-515).
The crate MUST keep forbid(unsafe_code) and deny(missing_docs), MSRV 1.85, edition 2021 (CON-201, CON-202, CON-102).
Security Baseline CON-516 is NOT APPLICABLE - no database, cache, or query surface. CON-513, CON-517, and CON-518 are also not applicable: no server responses, markup, or browser sessions.

edgeCases.description: Callback state does not match the stored value

edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Provider error surfaced as Auth; the store is not written.
Provider error surfaced verbatim, never silently rewritten.
Typed error telling the caller to re-authorize; no panic.

edgeCases.description: Two callers refresh the same record concurrently
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: At most one network refresh per client; last write wins and is documented.

edgeCases.description: Clock returns a time before the recorded issue time
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Expiry treated as elapsed; one refresh occurs.

edgeCases.description: Non-HTTPS token endpoint override that is not loopback
Provider returns an unrecognised error body
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: WirekitError::Api with the status and a redacted message; the body is never echoed.
Authorization URL still built; the provider response surfaces as Auth, never a silent retry.

risks.description: Google requires app verification for sensitive scopes, delaying M2 (catalogue/28 open question 3).
risks.mitigation: Scopes are caller-supplied; each module requests only its own.

risks.description: Refresh-token storage is security-critical and lives outside the crate.
risks.mitigation: The trait boundary is documented and the in-memory store is marked non-durable.

risks.description: Changing google_lsa to accept a token source could break callers.

risks.mitigation: EC-005 documents single-flight per client; a shared store needs an implementor-level lock.
